input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: The single-file wrapping check was changed from `isinstance(filename, str)` to `isinstance(filename, os.PathLike)`, so a plain `str` path is no longer wrapped in a tuple.
- rationale: Trigger: calling `click.edit(filename="notes.txt")` with a plain string. A str is not os.PathLike, so the branch is skipped and the str is passed to `ed.edit_files(filenames=...)`. edit_files iterates it, so the editor is invoked with individual characters ('n', 'o', 't', ...) as filenames instead of the single file. Impact: the most common single-file form of edit now opens the wrong files or fails, a regression for existing callers.
critique: The finding names the same faulty operation: the wrapping check was changed to test for os.PathLike, so a plain str is not wrapped. It also gives the same consequence: edit_files iterates the string, so each character becomes a filename. This matches the labeled mechanism and failure path.
